title: Jack Smith Dismisses Classified Documents Case After Trump Election Win
description_short: Jack Smith Dismisses Classified Documents Case After Trump Election Win
description_medium: After Trump won the 2024 election, Special Counsel Jack Smith asked to dismiss the Florida classified-documents prosecution under Justice Department policy against prosecuting a sitting president. The case concerned Trump’s retention of government records at Mar-a-Lago and alleged efforts to obstruct their recovery. The dismissal ended the federal prosecution without a trial or ruling on the allegations.
description_long: In November 2024, Special Counsel Jack Smith asked the courts to dismiss the federal classified-documents case against Trump after his election victory. The request relied on Justice Department policy that a sitting president cannot be prosecuted while in office. The case concerned hundreds of government documents retained at Mar-a-Lago after Trump left office, including sensitive national-security records, and alleged efforts to obstruct their recovery. Judge Aileen Cannon had dismissed the prosecution earlier; prosecutors were appealing that decision when Smith sought to end the case. The dismissal meant the allegations would not be tested at trial in this federal proceeding. It was a decision about prosecutorial policy and the transition to a second Trump term, not a finding that the underlying conduct did or did not occur. The source record does not describe the separate handling of the documents or any later proceedings. This entry records the request and its effect on the case without treating the dismissal as an exoneration.

title: Trump Retweets White Supremacist Fabricated Black Crime Statistics
description_short: Trump Retweets White Supremacist Fabricated Black Crime Statistics
description_medium: On November 22, 2015, Trump retweeted a graphic falsely claiming that Black Americans committed 81% of murders of white victims. FactCheck.org reported that the FBI data showed a much lower figure, about 15%. The graphic came from a white-supremacist account. When asked about checking the statistic, Trump said, “Am I gonna check every statistic?” The episode amplified false racial crime data to his large audience.
description_long: Trump retweeted a graphic on November 22, 2015, that falsely claimed Black Americans were responsible for 81% of murders of white victims. FactCheck.org compared the graphic with FBI data and found the figure was about 15%, not 81%. The post originated from an account associated with white-supremacist content and remained online after news organizations challenged it. When Fox News host Bill O’Reilly asked about the accuracy of the statistics, Trump responded, “Am I gonna check every statistic?” The event mattered because a candidate with a large audience circulated a false racial claim without first verifying it, then publicly minimized the need to check such material. The supplied record does not establish that Trump created the graphic or that he endorsed every view of its source. It documents the retweet, the factual correction, and his response, without adding unsupported claims about intent.

description_medium: Trump’s January 2025 executive order directed the Pentagon to discharge transgender service members. description_long: Trump signed an executive order on January 27, 2025, declaring that transgender identity conflicted with military service and directing the Pentagon to remove transgender service members. Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth’s May 8, 2025 memo gave active-duty personnel until June 6 to separate voluntarily or face involuntary discharge. An appeals court panel ruled on June 1, 2026, that the policy appeared to be driven by a desire to harm a politically unpopular group and therefore violated equal-protection principles, but the policy remained in effect while further review continued. description_long: Trump signed an executive order on May 11, 2017, establishing the Presidential Advisory Commission on Election Integrity, co-chaired by Kansas Secretary of State Kris Kobach.
